title: John Kirby's group and McKinney's Cotton Pickers
summary: Crawford discusses John Kirby's small band showing Lunceford's influence and wonders how McKinney's Cotton Pickers gathered such musicians.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: What did you think of -- how did you like John Kirby? Did you ever play with him?
Well, not too much. Because, -- he was a good bass player, that was a good bass player.
Well, sometimes it seems to me that his small group seems to have been very influenced by the Lunceford band.
Some of the arrangements -- I was listening to them not too long ago, it seemed like he --
Well, that was the Greatest Little

Band in the land." Yes, that band -- and McKinney's Cotton Pickers, back in Detroit. Now, how did he assemble all those great musicians in his band? Fathead on alto, even got Don Redman in there. We used to call him the Little Giant. Yeah, Little Giant. And he had -- and I don't know what instrument McKinney played. I think he was formerly a drummer, but he had a great, sensational drummer in there -- Cubie Austin. Great press roll man. Yes, McKinney you didn't see, hardly ever. He was just the boss. But -- he was just the boss of the band, McKinney's Cotton Pickers.
